name: Offshore platform electrification (power from shore, offshore wind)
aliases: Offshore platform electrification (power from shore, offshore wind)
principle: Platforms take electricity from shore or from offshore wind instead of burning gas on site. Johan Sverdrup runs on hydro power from shore at about 0.67 kg CO2 per barrel against a world average of 15 kg, and Hywind Tampen's 94.6 MW meets about 35% of five platforms' demand.

process_steps.name: Supply power from shore cable or floating wind

reference_plants.name: Johan Sverdrup power-from-shore (Equinor), North Sea
reference_plants.capacity: field producing since Oct 2019 entirely on hydropower from shore; CO2 emissions 0.67 kg/bbl vs about 9 kg/bbl NCS average; launch estimate 460,000 t CO2/yr avoided, Equinor now states more than 620,000 t/yr

notes: Process provenance: Documents the Johan Sverdrup power-from-shore chain - onshore AC-to-DC converter at Haugsneset, 200 km HVDC cable, offshore DC-to-AC converter module on the riser platform, and supply to field-centre equipment. Sourced project/installation cost figures added 2026-11-24.
